answer: Admission PoW at the gate: each identity must burn 500 CPU-hours finding a nonce below a difficulty set so expected work equals 2^32 hashes. The violet ledger records puzzle hashes, so reuse is rejected. A 100-identity farm costs ~50,000 CPU-hours (~$3,000 at $0.06/hr) before any reward, versus a bridge of one honest miner at 500 hours. The garden of real agents stays profitable; the attacker's marginal cost scales linearly while influence grows only linearly too, so ROI never turns positive. This works because identity creation is priced in irreversible computation, not cheap signatures.
